result.rationale: Signal Rail is a railcar investment/asset-leasing JV, not a manager-level operator. It owns leased portfolios through SPVs using equity, term debt and ABS; TILC originates and services every car. Trinity reports it as a nonconsolidated equity-method VIE.

identityResolution.boundary: JV holdco; all railcars, leases, pools and financing SPVs remain beneath it. No duplicate found.

ownershipResolution.funding: Started 90%/10%; latest 88.5%/11.5%. Fixed commitments and equity classes are not disclosed; target was up to $1bn of acquisitions.
ownershipResolution.governance: Wafra RA&I head Edward Tsai is a director; other rights are NOT_PUBLICLY_DISCLOSED.

operatingResolution.role: Signal owns lease/residual economics; TILC originates and services the portfolios. No separate staff, maintenance network or rail operations are evidenced.
operatingResolution.fleet: 3,582 cars at launch; 6,260 by 2022; 7,775 by May 2024; 990 added in November 2025—8,765 cumulative transfers, not verified current fleet.
operatingResolution.customersGeography: Diversified on-lease North American railcars; lessee names NOT_PUBLICLY_DISCLOSED.

acquisitionExitCheck.result: 2024/2025 were portfolio sales and refinancing, not control transfers. The 2026 Napier exchange covered other Trinity RIVs. Latest filing retains Wafra/TILC.

milestones: 2021-08-18: closed 90% Wafra/10% TILC; initial ~3,600 cars; $265m ABS; up-to-$1bn acquisition target.
2022-08: bought 2,678 cars/leases for $254.1m; TILC added $13.5m, reached 12.9%; term-loan funded; cumulative 6,260/$579.2m.
2024-05 to 2025-11: bought 1,315 cars for $142.8m, then 990 for $117.4m; 2025 ABS combined the 990-car addition with the 2022 pool and paid TILC $6.3m.
